questions.question: What kind of mention does extract_mentions create for the token "He"?
options: A nominal mention with head company
An organization mention with plural features
A pronoun mention with masculine singular features
No mention because pronouns are ignored
questions.explanation: PRONOUNS maps he to gender m, number sg, and type prp.

questions.question: What gender does infer_gender("Jordan Lee") return?
options: m, because every two-word name is masculine
f, because the last name is Lee
n, because names are always treated as objects
u, because Jordan is not in the hand-written first-name lists
questions.explanation: The helper examines the first token and returns u when it is absent from FEMALE_FIRST and MALE_FIRST.

questions.question: What agreement score does a singular unknown-gender pronoun receive against a singular candidate?
questions.explanation: Matching number adds 1.0, and an unknown gender on either side adds another 1.0.

questions.question: What does recency_score favor among otherwise similar antecedents?
options: The candidate that appears earliest in the document
A candidate with a smaller sentence and token distance from the pronoun
A candidate with the longest surface string
A candidate that has never been extracted as a mention
questions.explanation: The score is the negative distance from mention span to candidate span, so nearer previous mentions score higher.

questions.question: Which antecedents can resolve consider for a pronoun?
options: Only mentions in the same token position
Every later mention in the document
Earlier named-entity or nominal mentions, not earlier pronouns
Only candidates whose text is exactly the pronoun
questions.explanation: The candidates comprehension scans mentions[:i] and keeps types ne and nominal.

questions.question: How does clusters join two mentions after resolve links them?
options: It concatenates their strings and sorts characters
It deletes the pronoun from the mention list
It assigns every mention to one global cluster
Union-find links their object IDs and groups mentions by the resulting root
questions.explanation: clusters initializes one parent per mention, unions linked pairs, and collects texts sharing a root.
